It explains how we collect and use information through use of i) our AI phone receptionist to answer calls and set appointments (the “ AI Receptionist ”; ii) a Subscriber dashboard, software and applications integrated with a Subscriber’s existing systems (collectively, the “ Application ”); and iii) heyrosie.com and other websites or online channels we own or operate (collectively, the “ Site ”) (altogether, with the Site and Application, the “ Services ”). Any use of our Services is subject to this Privacy Notice and our Terms of Service, including its applicable limitations on damages and the provisions regarding resolution of disputes.
Please read this Privacy Notice carefully to understand how we collect and use personal information. We may provide additional notices about our privacy practices, each of which will be considered to form part of this Privacy Notice. YOU CONSENT TO OUR PRIVACY PRACTICES BY INDICATING YOUR CONSENT WHERE THE OPTION IS MADE AVAILABLE OR USING OUR SERVICES IN ANY MANNER. If you do not agree with this Privacy Notice, do not access or use our Services.
This Privacy Notice does not apply to our Subscribers’ collection or use of Personal Information through our Services or otherwise. Callers should contact the business they called for privacy support.
Rosie may update this Privacy Notice from time to time. We will notify you about material changes to this Privacy Notice through the Services or by email and we will collect your consent to these changes to the extent required by applicable law. Rosie Subscribers and prospective Subscribers may contact Rosie with questions at [email protected] .
1. Subscribers and Callers
This Privacy Notice does not apply to data collected by a third party, including the subscribing businesses and individuals that use an AI Receptionist to answer or make calls or perform other Services on their behalf (our “ Subscribers ”). Rosie provides the Services to our Subscribers, and each Subscriber determines how it will use the data collected from their Callers and other customers through the Services. Any processing of data by Rosie to train or develop AI technologies is governed by contracts with our Subscribers, not this Privacy Notice.
Rosie Subscribers that use the AI Receptionist may choose to collect and process Personal Information about their Callers or other customers. Each Subscriber is responsible for their own Personal Information collection and storing or processing that data on the Services. This includes AI Receptionist functionality, privacy settings, data management, giving notice and obtaining consent from Callers, and responding to Callers’ privacy inquiries. Callers should contact the Subscriber with any questions about their Personal Information on the Services.
2. “Personal Information” Defined
As used in this Privacy Notice, “ Personal Information ” is information that identifies, relates to, describes, references, is capable of being associated with, or could reasonably be linked, directly or indirectly, with a particular individual consumer or device, such as:
● Identifiers (e.g., name, email, telephone number, address, username);
● Sensitive Personal Information (e.g., biometrics like voice recordings, precise geolocation, health information, contents of messages when we are not the recipient; in some cases, information about a known child);
● Legally protected information (e.g., race, citizenship, marital status, sex);
● Employment-related information (e.g., current or past employment);
● Non-public educational information, including information protected under the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (20 U.S.C. § 1232g, 34 C.F.R. Part 99);
● Commercial information (e.g., products or services purchased, obtained, or considered, or other purchasing or consuming histories or tendencies);
● Internet or other similar activity (e.g., browsing history; content interactions); and
● Inferences drawn from Personal Information to create a profile about preferences, characteristics, trends, predispositions, behavior, attitudes, intelligence, and aptitudes.
Note that information may not be protected by privacy laws if it is: (i) publicly available (ii) aggregated, meaning data about a group or category of services or Callers from which individual identities and other Personal Information has been removed; or (iii) deidentified so that it cannot be easily linked back to the individual.

Rosie will only collect, use, retain, and disclose Personal Information as described in this section, and only as reasonably necessary and proportionate to provide the Services or for other purposes stated in this Privacy Notice or at the time of collection.
Rosie collects identifiers, commercial history, internet and similar activity from Callers and Subscribers, as well as sensitive information or other categories of Personal Information that a Caller chooses to include in their call. We collect this information with consent, with a legitimate interest, or as authorized or required by law.

Rosie reserves the right to refuse Subscriber instructions to collect or process Personal Information about another individual without their consent or in a manner or for a purpose that Rosie determines violates others’ privacy or publicity rights, or otherwise violates our Terms of Service, and such instructions may result in termination of Services at our option. Collected from Callers on behalf of a Subscriber. Our AI Receptionist collects Personal Information from Callers on behalf of our Subscribers.

The AI Receptionist will use the information to generate the Caller’s requested information or other outputs. Callers consent to this processing by submitting their Personal Information to the AI Receptionist.

If a Caller requests to set an appointment with a Subscriber, the Services will schedule the appointment on the Subscriber’s system. If the Subscriber uses text or email reminders, the Services will process the Caller’s Personal Information to generate and send those appointment reminders to the Caller.

Subscriber consents on behalf of itself and its Callers to Rosie’s processing of Caller Personal Information as described in this Privacy Notice. A Caller should contact the Subscriber with questions about Personal Information included in a conversation with an AI Receptionist.

5. Retention of Personal Information
As a service provider to our Subscribers, Rosie retains Personal Information about Callers until the Subscriber deletes it or instructs us to do so. Subscriber account information is retained while the account is active. We delete Subscriber account data 30 days after the Subscriber’s subscription is cancelled. Subscribers may retain Personal Information collected through the Services for different retention periods, subject to the Subscriber’s privacy practices.
Personal Information on our marketing lists is retained until you opt out or we determine that the information no longer serves our business purposes. For example, if you have never been a Subscriber and you do not interact with the marketing content we send you for two years, we will remove your Personal Information from our marketing lists. Other types of data are retained and disposed of according to our company policies. Rosie may retain Personal Information for longer if we feel it is necessary for legal or regulatory purposes.
When we no longer have a business need for your Personal Information, we will either delete, de-identify, or anonymize it whenever feasible. Where not feasible (such as data in our backup archives) we will securely store it and keep it isolated from further processing until it can be permanently deleted.
6. Third-Party Services
The Services may provide access or links to services offered by third parties. Please note that Rosie has no control over third-party websites, apps, devices, or systems, and you should exercise caution when deciding to disclose your Personal Information.

Rosie currently offers the Services in the United States and Canada. This section lists the privacy rights applicable to individuals under consumer privacy laws in the United States and Canada.
If you are a Caller, you must contact the Subscriber you called to exercise your privacy rights related to a conversation you had with an AI Receptionist. The notices in this section are provided to Callers as a courtesy only. The Subscriber you called is ultimately responsible for how it processes your Personal Information and for supporting your exercise of privacy rights.
United States. For those in the United States , consumer privacy is governed by federal privacy laws covering specific industries or data uses and more than a dozen state laws providing consumer privacy rights. Residents of states like California, Colorado, Connecticut, Nevada, Utah, Virginia, and other states that offer privacy protections may be entitled to some or all of the privacy rights listed below:
· Right to know. Rosie provides the required information for a consumer’s right to know in this Privacy Notice. We may provide you with additional notices about other ways we process your Personal Information through the Services or via email. Each Subscriber is separately responsible for providing its Callers with an explanation for the right to know.
· Right to reasonable expectations. You can expect Rosie to collect, use, or disclose your Personal Information responsibly and not for any other purpose other than as stated at the time of collection or described in this Privacy Notice. If we collect or use your Personal Information based on your consent, we will also notify you of any changes and will request your further consent as required by law. You may withdraw your consent at any time with reasonable notice by contacting [email protected] . Subscribers must set expectations for their Callers separately. Please contact the Subscriber you called to change or withdraw your consent.
· Right to accuracy, and the right to correct your Personal Information. You can correct or update your Personal Information held by Rosie by updating your account or by contacting [email protected] . However, we do not make any guarantee that Personal Information contained in our Subscribers’ data (including information collected by AI Receptionists) is accurate. Rosie must rely on our Subscribers to ensure that the data we process on the Subscriber’s behalf is current, complete and accurate. Please contact the Subscriber you called if you become aware that your Personal Information processed through our Services is not accurate.
· Right to access your Personal Information. Callers should contact the Subscriber they called to request access to their Personal Information processed via an AI Receptionist. Others may submit a request to Rosie to receive a copy of their Personal Information held by us. We will provide copies upon request where required by law, along with details about the types of Personal Information we process, why we process it, and any third parties we work with to collect Personal Information on our behalf. Certain laws may limit the scope or frequency of requests we must fulfill.
· Right to deletion. Callers should contact the Subscriber they called to request the deletion of their Personal Information. If Rosie collected your Personal Information for our own purposes, upon your request and when required by law, we will delete your Personal Information from our systems. This right is not absolute, and we may be entitled to retain and process your Personal Information despite your request. If you make this request, we balance certain legal, contractual, and business interests against your right to request the deletion of your Personal Information.
· Right to data portability. In some cases, we are required to provide your Personal Information to another organization at your request and in a structured, commonly used machine-readable format, so that the other organization can read and use it.
· No selling Personal Information. Rosie does not sell any Personal Information or share Personal Information with third parties for cross-contextual behavioral advertising purposes. Subscribers are free to sell or share Callers’ Personal Information according to the Subscriber’s own privacy practices. Please review the Subscriber’s privacy notice to learn more and to understand how to opt-out.
· Limited use and disclosure of sensitive Personal Information. Rosie does not collect sensitive Personal Information, and in no case will Rosie use or disclose sensitive Personal Information for the purpose of inferring characteristics about a consumer. Subscribers are free to collect Callers’ sensitive Personal Information, through the AI Receptionist or other means. Please review the Subscriber’s privacy notice to learn more and to understand how to opt-out.
· Right to non-discrimination. If you reside in a jurisdiction that extends a right to non-discrimination related to the exercise of privacy rights, we will not (i) deny you goods or services, (ii) charge you different prices or rates for goods or services, (iii) provide you a different level or quality of goods or services, (iv) retaliate against you as an employee, applicant for employment, or independent contractor; or (v) suggest that you may receive a different price or rate for goods or services or a different level or quality of goods or services, because you exercised your statutory right unless permitted by law.
· Right to disclosure of certain information. You may have a right to request information about how we collect and use your Personal Information, such as (i) the categories of Personal Information we have collected about you; (ii) the categories of sources for the Personal Information we have collected about you; (iii) our business purpose for collecting, using, disclosing, or selling that Personal Information, as applicable; and (iv) the categories of third parties with whom we disclose that Personal Information. Rosie does not sell or share your Personal Information, but if we did you could request two separate lists stating: (a) sales, identifying the Personal Information categories that each category of recipient purchased; and (b) sharing for a business purpose, identifying the Personal Information categories that each category of recipient obtained. Certain laws may limit the number or frequency of requests we must fulfill.
· Right to not be subject to automated decision-making and the right to opt out of profiling. Our Subscribers’ AI Receptionists leverage generative AI technologies that process data in a manner that may qualify as automated decision-making or profiling under privacy laws. Each Subscriber is responsible for this type of processing and for providing Callers with notice and a method to opt-out. A Caller can prevent their Personal Information from being processed in this manner by requesting human intervention through the Services or by discontinuing the call.
· Right to restrict processing. You may have the right to request that we restrict the processing of your Personal Information if (i) the data is inaccurate, (ii) the processing is unlawful, (iii) we no longer need the Personal Information, or (iv) you exercise your right to object. Your right to restrict may be limited to Personal Information that is sensitive in nature, or that is sold or shared for certain purposes. · Right to object. You may have the right to request, under certain circumstances and where we are required to do so by law, that we limit our processing of your Personal Information as you request.
· Right to disclosure of marketing information. If you are a resident of the State of California, California’s Shine the Light Act (Civil Code sections 1798.83-1798.84) entitles California consumers to request certain disclosures regarding Personal Information sharing with affiliates and/or third parties for marketing purposes.
· Health Data Rights. Rosie does not collect any health data. A Subscriber may choose to collect health data through the AI Receptionist or otherwise process health data through our Services. Please contact the Subscriber you called if you become aware that your Personal Information processed through our Services is not accurate.
· Right to access your Personal Information. Callers should contact the Subscriber they called to request access to their Personal Information processed via an AI Receptionist. 10. Rosie Data Security
Rosie has implemented and maintains reasonable security measures to secure Personal Information on our Services from accidental loss and unauthorized access, use, alteration, and disclosure. All data is securely stored in a cloud environment and encrypted using AWS AES256 encryption. Rosie personnel are required to follow security protocols and are trained to handle sensitive data. Data and systems are subject to regular backups and audits. Our service providers are contractually bound to adhere to the same security protections. Rosie has policies and protocols in place to respond to security incidents in compliance with our customer agreements and applicable law. Our security measures are appropriate to the volume, scope, and nature of the Personal Information processed and designed to meet our duty of care.
Subscribers are responsible for securely storing and processing Personal Data on the Subscriber’s information systems and through their use of our Services. We cannot guarantee the security of information transmitted over the Internet. Any data transmissions are at the risk of the person initiating the transfer.
